title: Diataxis: a systematic framework for technical documentation authoring
author: Daniele Procida

record.source: The four-quadrant documentation framework, which this repository keeps reinventing under other names. Read for the axes rather than for the four names. It reaches this repository twice: as the frame adopted in `docs/adr/documentation_quadrants.md`, and as the section vendored through pstack's `technical-writing` skill into `.agents/skills/project-documentation/references/organization.md`.
record.kept: The two axes and the rule that a document serves one form: a reader either acts or studies, and the material is either acquired or applied. One quadrant per document.
record.rewritten: The four names are this repository's, and the mapping from quadrant to corpus is the adoption recorded at `docs/adr/documentation_quadrants.md`: learning is `docs/development`, a how-to is the instruction surface rather than a document, understanding is `docs/adr`, and information is `docs/reference`. A how-to written as a document is the case the mapping rules out, because a reader who must be present for a procedure makes the document stale.
record.added: Two shapes the framework does not name. The advisor is invoked like a how-to and prescribes nothing, so it is a diagnostic shape inside that quadrant. The judgement is applied mid-work and consulted by nobody, so it sits outside the four, with the session records.
record.dropped: The pedagogical framing and the map of tutorials, which serve a reader learning a tool for the first time rather than an agent working in it.
